collection.critical_edition: Burnet, Platonis Opera IV (1902), via Perseus
collection.search_terms: plato republic politeia sun divided line cave allegory idea of the good form beyond being dialectic education shorey laurenziana
collection.description: The central images of Plato's Republic, the Sun, the Divided Line and the Cave, each Stephanus subsection shown on the page of the 12th-century Florence manuscript Laur. Plut. 80.19 that carries it, with Burnet's Greek and Paul Shorey's English.

texts.title: Plato, Republic 6.506d-511e: the Sun and the Divided Line
texts.source: Florence, Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Plut. 80.19 fol. 72v-75r (Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Teca digitale (IIIF)) + Burnet's Greek (Perseus) + Paul Shorey's English (Loeb, 1935, Perseus)
texts.description: Socrates' images of the Good: the sun, offspring of the Good, gives the visible world light and growth as the Good gives the intelligible world truth and being, itself 'beyond being'; then the line divided into four parts, from images to intelligence. Shown on the 12th-century Florence manuscript Laur. Plut. 80.19.

texts.title: Plato, Republic 7.514a-521b: the Allegory of the Cave
texts.source: Florence, Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Plut. 80.19 fol. 75r-78v (Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Teca digitale (IIIF)) + Burnet's Greek (Perseus) + Paul Shorey's English (Loeb, 1935, Perseus)
texts.description: The opening of Republic book 7: prisoners chained in a cave see only shadows; one is freed, turned round and dragged up into the sunlight, sees the sun itself, and must go back down. Education as the turning of the soul, and the duty of the philosopher to return. Shown on the 12th-century Florence manuscript Laur. Plut. 80.19.
